claims.statement: The vaccination reminder letter policy increased full adherence to the Danish Childhood Vaccination Program at age 3 among children who were non-adherent at age 2 by 8.7 percentage points.

treatment.label: Reminder letter (the vaccination reminder letter policy)

register_source.value: Not a register variable: treatment assignment is defined by the child's second-year birthday relative to the reform date 15 May 2014. Eligibility for a letter was determined by the health authorities from the Danish Vaccination Register; the paper names no Statistics Denmark register code.

definition.value: Receipt of a vaccination reminder letter at age 2. Treatment is assigned sharply by the reform date: Ti = 1{si >= 0}, where si is child i's second-year birthday relative to 15 May 2014. From 15 May 2014, parents of a child who at age 2 lacks at least one scheduled vaccination receive a letter stating that, according to the records, the child lacks at least one vaccination, followed by a table of the vaccination schedule with red markings; it contains no pro-vaccination campaigning other than stating the general purpose of the programme. Parents receive only one letter regardless of how many rounds the child lacks.

timing.value: At the child's second birthday (age 2); the policy cut-off is 15 May 2014

outcome.label: Indicator for full adherence in the Danish Childhood Vaccination Program at age 3 (all scheduled vaccinations received by age 3)

register_source.value: Statistics Denmark administrative data: children's vaccination history including the dates for each vaccination round; the paper names no register code

definition.value: 'My main outcome is an indicator for full adherence in the program at age 3.' Below age 2 adherent children have four vaccinations scheduled, at 3, 5, 12 and 15 months after birth; the indicator equals one if the child has all scheduled vaccinations at age 3.

timing.value: At age 3, one year after the reminder letter is sent at age 2

units.value: Proportion / indicator for full adherence at age 3; a coefficient of 0.087 is 8.7 percentage points

magnitude.interpretation: The reminder letter policy increases adherence with 8.7%-points in the group of non-adherent children at age 2; this is also the estimated share of responsive parents (8.7%), against 19.2% delaying and 72.1% non-responsive. In the introduction the author describes it as increasing 'adherence by 50% for non-adherent children a year after receiving the reminder letter'.

estimand.time_horizon: Adherence measured at age 3, one year after the letter is sent at age 2

key_assumptions.assumption: No manipulation: individuals have imprecise control over their treatment status, i.e. parents cannot systematically manipulate the child's second-year birthday relative to the 15 May 2014 cut-off, nor their eligibility for a letter.
key_assumptions.supported_by: McCrary (2008) density test: estimated jump in the log density of 0.055 with a standard error of 0.061 (Appendix Figure A3); no visible bunching around the cut-off (Appendix Figure A2); the share of eligible (non-adherent) children is stable at 20-25% through the period (Appendix Figure A4); the birth determining the running variable occurred two years before an unexpected policy.

key_assumptions.assumption: For reading parental responses as causes for non-adherence: (1) every parent intended to receive a reminder letter successfully does so, reads the reminder and understands the content, and (2) only inattentive parents respond to the reminder letter.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The author calls these 'strict conditions' and discusses threats to each in Section 3.2; condition (2) is informally assessed by the timing of the response (Appendix Figure A7), by unchanged Google search trends for 'vaccination' and 'side-effects vaccination' (Appendix Figure A8) and by the heterogeneity results. treatment.label: Reminder letter (the vaccination reminder letter policy)

definition.value: Receipt of a vaccination reminder letter at age 2. Treatment is assigned sharply by the reform date: Ti = 1{si >= 0}, where si is child i's second-year birthday relative to 15 May 2014. From 15 May 2014, parents of a child who at age 2 lacks at least one scheduled vaccination receive a letter stating that, according to the records, the child lacks at least one vaccination, followed by a table of the vaccination schedule with red markings; it contains no pro-vaccination campaigning other than stating the general purpose of the programme. Parents receive only one letter regardless of how many rounds the child lacks.
